jobs.description:
Position Description

Position Overview:

The Harris County Fire Marshal's Office (HCFMO) is seeking a skilled and motivated Geographic Information System (GIS) Specialist to join the Operations Support Bureau. This role supports fire investigation, hazmat operations, emergency management, and multi-agency coordination through the development and maintenance of geospatial tools, data systems, internal GIS web applications, and analytical products.

The GIS Specialist will design, maintain, and analyze spatial datasets; produce maps, dashboards, and reports; and serve as the HCFMO's primary geospatial resource in support of operational, investigative, and strategic decision-making. The position interfaces regularly with fire, EMS, and law enforcement agency partners across Harris County, and may support Emergency Operations Center (EOC) events.

The ideal candidate is technically proficient in ESRI products, comfortable with data integration and automation, able to support configuration-level maintenance of internal mapping applications (e.g., layer setup, symbology, access/permissions settings), and capable of translating complex geospatial information into clear, actionable products for command staff, public officials, and partner agencies.

Duties and Responsibilities:

Geospatial Analysis & Decision Support
Perform spatial analysis to support fire investigation, hazmat incident response, deployment planning, prevention, and risk reduction activities.
Develop and maintain data layers and geodatabases integrating internal records (incident, investigation, inspection) with external datasets (county parcels, Census, CAD feeds, utility infrastructure).
Analyze incident patterns, coverage gaps, response time performance, and risk density to support strategic and operational planning by command staff.
Produce recommendations and briefings derived from geospatial analysis for use by the Fire Marshal, division leadership, and partner agencies.
Evaluate data and access requirements for internal geospatial applications and recommend configuration changes to layers, symbology, or user permissions to better support analytical and operational needs.

Data Management & Quality Assurance
Design, build, and maintain geodatabases from multiple internal and external data sources in various formats.
Ensure spatial data accuracy, integrity, and consistency through systematic quality control and error-checking procedures.
Maintain geospatial data feeds required by Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD) systems used by the HCFMO and regional dispatch partners.
Develop and document data standards, coding structures, and metadata to support business continuity and interoperability.
Apply change-control practices (e.g., testing and validating configuration or data changes before deployment to production systems) to minimize disruption to operational users.
Support maintenance of user and facility access permissions within internal geospatial applications, ensuring data governance and access-control settings remain accurate and current.

Cartography & Application Management
Produce and maintain print and digital maps for fire investigation, hazmat operations, fire prevention, special events, and administrative use.
Create and maintain ArcGIS Online web maps, dashboards, Survey123 forms, and mobile mapping applications used by field personnel.
Provide geospatial products and field support during large-scale incidents.
Maintain and update the mobile mapping environment for fire investigators and inspectors.
Configure and maintain layer settings, symbology, and feature-service connections within HCFMO's internal geospatial application(s), coordinating with technical/IT staff as needed for deeper platform-level changes.

Reporting & Data Visualization
Design and maintain operational and strategic reports and dashboards tailored to varied audiences, from field supervisors to elected officials.
Translate complex spatial data into clear visualizations (maps, charts, heat maps, infographics) that support retention and informed decision-making.
Integrate GIS products with other software platforms to support enterprise data workflows.

Coordination & Consultation
Serve as the HCFMO's GIS representative in regional geospatial working groups and inter-agency coordination bodies.
Collaborate with HCFMO divisions (investigations, hazmat, fire prevention, operations) and partner agencies to identify GIS needs and solutions.
Provide technical consultation and training to HCFMO personnel on GIS tools, data applications, and spatial query methods.
Support integration of GIS capabilities with UAS (drone) operations for incident mapping, post-fire documentation, and aerial data collection.

Automation & Workflow Development
Develop Python scripts, Model Builder workflows, and other automation tools to streamline routine data processing and reporting.
Evaluate and recommend new geospatial technologies, extensions, and integrations to improve HCFMO workflows.
Document all procedures, scripts, and automated workflows to ensure knowledge continuity.

Requirements

Education and Experience:

Bachelor's degree in Geographic Information Systems/Science, Geography, Computer Science, Emergency Management, or a closely related field

OR

An Associates degree plus
Three (3) years of directly relevant full-time experience may be substituted for the bachelor's degree requirement

WITH

Minimum three (3) years of full-time experience in GIS analysis, data management, and cartography.
Demonstrated experience using ESRI ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, and related extensions (Spatial Analyst, Network Analyst).
Experience creating and maintaining geodatabases and ensuring geospatial data quality and integrity.
Experience producing maps, dashboards, and analytical reports for operational or decision-making purposes.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

GIS concepts, analytical techniques, and digital mapping principles.
ESRI product suite: ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online/Enterprise, and extensions.
Geodatabase design, maintenance, and spatial data quality assurance methods.
Statistical and analytical methods applicable to spatial data (clustering, network analysis, proximity, density).
CAD system geospatial data requirements and integration methods.
Emergency management frameworks including ICS/NIMS; EOC operations and GISS function.
GPS concepts and field data collection procedures.
Data governance and access-control principles as applied to enterprise GIS applications.
Perform complex spatial analysis to support tactical, operational, and strategic decision-making in a public safety environment.
Produce clear, accurate, and audience-appropriate maps, reports, and visualizations under time pressure.
Manage multiple concurrent projects and prioritize effectively in a dynamic, operational environment.
Explain technical geospatial concepts clearly to non-technical users, including command staff, investigators, and partner agency personnel.
Work independently with minimal supervision while maintaining alignment with organizational priorities.
Establish effective working relationships with internal divisions and external partner agencies.
Respond and deploy for large-scale incidents, EOC activations, or other deployments as directed.

NOTICE:
Applicants for this position will be subject to a criminal background check that includes being fingerprinted. This applies to any position with network access to Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS) or access to an area where CJIS is received, maintained, or stored either manually or electronically (i.e. custodian, maintenance).

Convictions, probation, or deferred adjudication for any Felony, and any Class A Misdemeanor.

Proficiency with Python scripting or GIS Model Builder for workflow automation.
Experience with SQL, relational databases, Microsoft SQL Server, or Power BI.
Familiarity with UAV/UAS operations and integration of aerial imagery into GIS workflows.
Experience with AutoCAD, Survey123, QuickCapture, or similar field data collection platforms.

jobs.title: GIS Specialist
jobs.description:
Ting Internet is a leading fiber Internet provider in the United States, delivering future-proof internet in over a dozen Ting Towns across the country.
As part of Tucows (NASDAQ:TCX, TSX:TC), Ting is backed by outstanding resources and talent. We embrace a people-first philosophy that is rooted in respect, trust, and flexibility. We believe that whatever works for our employees is what works best for us. 
The work we do genuinely changes lives. If this sounds exciting, we’d love to hear from you!
Position Overview
As a fixed-line Fiber provider, Ting relies on knowing where our customers are and where our fiber is so we can bring those two things together. GIS (Geographic Information Systems) is all about modelling real-world objects as data that other digital systems can work with. Your job as a GIS Specialist is to ensure the data in these systems does match the real world, and then use this data to answer business questions.
Key Responsibilities
Manage the GIS ticket queue to support our internal users Solve suspected data issues such as address availability check errors by looking at plant drawings, maps, aerial and street photographs, and other sources of data to determine if our system might have the wrong data. Correct as necessary, or confirm an unexpected case is in fact accurate.
Add newly created addresses. If a building adds an apartment, or a new building is constructed on an empty lot, the new address needs to be added to our system.

Audit partner address releases Our partner providers invoice us for passed addresses, serviced addresses, and other incremental services that need to be checked against what they have actually provided to us. Using reports, tracking sheets, and automation tools that you will help to design, ensure that our numbers match their numbers.
Receive address delivery batches from partners when new areas are constructed. This data must be checked and ingested into our database so customers can place orders.  We also need to track releases so we can account for the pro-rated invoice the following month. Partner deliveries also need to be checked against map data to ensure they didn’t deliver addresses that don’t exist, or deliver the same one twice.

As-Built and Records Maintenance Ingest as-built records from partner and organic construction into our systems of record. Convert from various CAD formats to structured data formats that can be ingested by IQGeo and other systems.
Maintain the data sets in IQGeo and other systems in response to network changes, additional plant placements, and otherwise ensure that our system of record always reflects the actual state of our plant, and the plant of our partner networks.

Periodic Tasks: Work with the design team to correctly update IQGeo with plant moves or other changes to the physical network that need to be reflected back here.
Twice a year, produce output to support our FCC reporting. This process is very automatable, but it still requires human judgment to define how the process should work and to ensure our filings happen accurately. On a different twice-annual basis, download the aggregated FCC data that becomes publicly available and ingest it back into our database so we can use it for business intelligence.
Use database queries and other geospatial tools to generate reports for internal stakeholders.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities 
Geography was actually fun for you. Maybe you enjoy looking at maps and exploring real places without leaving your desk.
Attention to detail! This is the most important skill, as the accuracy of our data affects every downstream process.
Familiarity with IQGeo. This is the main tool used by the GIS team for viewing plant data and the addresses we manage (organic, partners with no system of their own). This is a fairly intuitive web-based tool, but has some nuances to it.
Experience with SQL queries, especially PostGIS. Our underlying database is PostGIS. Being able to construct an SQL query to produce aggregate data or work with batches can save a great deal of manual work.
Experience with other GIS tools such as ArcGIS Pro. This is another ancillary tool used to store map layers and do other data aggregations. Not strictly necessary, but a nice-to-have.
You like to help others, but not necessarily be on the front-lines of customer service. You will be supporting Ting people internally only.
You are a good self-starter and can work independently. The work is largely asynchronous, but we need to provide a high service level to our internal customers and make sure nothing falls through the cracks.
You have the tenacity to get work done, but are just lazy enough to look at repetitive tasks and think about how better tools could take the grunt work out of it.

Qualifications  Completed Post-secondary education in Applied Geography, Geographic Information Systems or equivalent experience

Matternet is building the future of delivery with autonomous drone networks that move critical goods faster, cleaner, and at lower cost. We work with partners across healthcare, logistics, food, and retail to deliver everything from medical items to everyday essentials, safely and reliably.

As a Ground Support Crew Member, you keep the network running. You will be based in Northridge, working across our active delivery sites, preparing aircraft, loading orders, and acting as the link between our part 135 Operations Partner and the restaurants and shops our drones fly for. This is a hands-on, field-based role with real responsibility from day one.

Your shift starts before the first flight. You inspect the aircraft, verify equipment, and communicate with the remote ops center to begin the day. When an order comes in from a partner restaurant or shop, you make it happen and see the flight off.

In this role, you will:

Support the launch of new operations sites, including onboarding new customers and enrolling them in our delivery program
Conduct pre- and post-flight aircraft inspections per approved procedures; maintain accurate airworthiness and maintenance records
Prepare and load payloads for each flight; verify order accuracy and packaging integrity at the point of handoff from merchant partners
Operate and service ground equipment and charging systems
Act as the on-site liaison between remote operations center and partner restaurants and shops, coordinating flight schedules, communicating delays, and resolving ground-level issues in real time
Troubleshoot and document mechanical and electrical discrepancies; escalate faults through the proper maintenance release process
Enforce site safety protocols, manage non-crew personnel around the aircraft, and report occurrences through Safety Management System
Complete Operator certification and all required recurrent training to maintain active status

Requirements

FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate (current and valid)
Hands-on experience with mechanical and/or electrical systems; aviation, automotive, robotics, or industrial background all considered
Ability to follow and execute written SOPs accurately in a safety-critical environment
Clear communicator; comfortable coordinating between a remote operations team and on-site merchant partners
Comfortable working outdoors, on your feet, across variable shift hours including early mornings and weekends
Ability to comply with the Company's FAA/DOT-mandated drug and alcohol testing program (see Drug & Alcohol Testing below)
Based or able to work onsite in Los Angeles, CA

Preferred qualifications:

Multi-rotor UAS operating experience beyond Part 107 certification
Experience in a Part 135, Part 145, or other FAA-regulated operating environment
Experience authoring or revising controlled documents (SOPs, maintenance procedures, inspection checklists)
Manned aviation background (student pilot, PPL, CPL, or military flight experience)

Work Environment

This is an on-site, field-based role operating from Ground Control Stations and active delivery sites in and around Northridge (Los Angeles, CA)
The work will be predominately outdoors with exposure to sun, heat, wind, cold, and noise for the duration of a shift.
Shifts may include early mornings, weekends, holidays, and on-call availability
Travel will be required between local operating sites and to support new route validation

The physical demands described below are representative of those that must be met to successfully perform the essential functions of this role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these functions.

Stand, walk, and remain on your feet for the majority of a shift, often on outdoor and uneven surfaces
Frequently lift, carry, and position aircraft, batteries, payloads, and ground equipment weighing up to approximately 50 lbs; occasionally more with assistance
Bend, stoop, kneel, crouch, and reach to inspect aircraft, load payloads, and service ground equipment
Use hand tools and perform tasks requiring manual dexterity and fine motor control
Sufficient near and distance visual acuity and hearing to inspect aircraft, monitor operations, and communicate on-site and by radio
Communicate clearly and exchange accurate information verbally and in writing with the Air Operations team and merchant partners
Work safely around aircraft, moving rotors, charging systems, and ground support equipment, and tolerate outdoor weather conditions
This position is subject to DOT/FAA drug and alcohol testing, including pre-employment and random testing. Federal law also requires us to review an applicant's DOT drug and alcohol testing history prior to hire

Benefits

At Matternet, we're advancing a new era of logistics, one where autonomous drones deliver what matters faster, cleaner, and more efficiently. We know our mission is challenging, but it's worth it, and we are committed to taking care of the people who make it possible.

About The Position

The Riverside County Flood Control and Water Conservation District seeks an Regulatory and Environmental Planner (Associate Environmental Specialist). This position is assigned to the Regulatory Division in Riverside and is comparable to traditional Environmental Planner roles.

To learn more about this position click here to view a video.

Individuals in this role will have prior planning experience and will support the District with a broad range of responsibilities related to environmental compliance under laws such as the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), the Clean Water Act, the state and federal Endangered Species Acts, and the California Fish and Game Code. Key duties include performing and reviewing technical analyses for flood control projects to assess environmental impacts; conducting field survey; and recommending appropriate mitigation measures in accordance with applicable environmental regulations and procedures.

Additional responsibilities include preparing and reviewing environmental documents (e.g., CEQA analyses), as well as regulatory permit applications under Sections 404, 401, and 1600. Associate Regulatory and Environmental Planners may also be tasked with developing Requests for Proposals (RFPs), overseeing consultant deliverables, and coordinating with internal divisions and external agencies at the local, state, federal, or tribal level. This role also involves providing technical support to Project Managers and mentoring Assistant or Junior level staff.

The ideal candidate will have experience serving as a project manager or task lead in a similar role at an environmental or engineering focused consulting firm or within a public works or land use/planning agency, and a background in preparing or reviewing technical studies, including NEPA or CEQA environmental documents (e.g., Environmental Impact Reports, Mitigated Negative Declarations, Negative Declarations, Notices of Exemption). Experience in preparing, reviewing, or negotiating regulatory permits from the California Department of Fish and Wildlife, Regional Water Quality Control Boards, and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers is highly desirable. Familiarity with projects located within the Western Riverside County Multiple Species Habitat Conservation Plan (MSHCP) and/or the Coachella Valley MSHCP is also preferred.

The most competitive candidates will demonstrate a solid understanding of the principles and practices of urban and environmental planning, flood control, and land development. They should have experience interpreting and implementing relevant environmental laws and regulations, including CEQA, the National Historic Preservation Act, Assembly Bill 52 (AB 52), the Federal and California Endangered Species Acts, the Clean Water Act (Sections 401 and 404), and the California Fish and Game Code. Strong analytical, report-writing, project/task management and verbal communication skills are essential, along with proficiency in Microsoft Office programs (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, etc.). Candidates should also be capable of reading and interpreting environmental documents and technical reports (Aquatic Resources Delineation Reports, biological resources reports, cultural resources reports, etc.), hydrology and hydraulics studies, drainage plans, and development proposals.

Track II – Regulatory And Environmental Planning

Positions assigned to the Regulatory Division ensure compliance with environmental regulations related to long-range planning, facility design and construction, maintenance and repair projects, and developing and managing mitigation sites/conservation lands. Incumbents apply regulatory requirements pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), the state and federal Endangered Species Acts, California Fish and Game Code Section 1600, Clean Water Act Sections 401 and 404, and the Western Riverside County and the Coachella Valley Multiple Species Habitat Conservation Plans (MSHCPs). Incumbents in this track assist with CEQA compliance, species and habitat management, regulatory permitting acquisition, negotiation and compliance, prepare or review environmental documents and technical studies, and coordinate with internal staff, public agencies, consultants, and other stakeholders as needed to ensure effective project delivery.

To learn more about the position or the Regulatory Division at the District, here.

Meet The Team!

The Riverside County Flood Control and Water Conservation District provides for the control and conservation of flood and storm waters and for the protection of watercourses, watersheds, public highways, life and property from damage within its boundaries.

Utilize technical knowledge of environmental laws and regulations to support long-range planning, capital project development, facility operations and maintenance, and developing and managing mitigation sites/conservation lands.
Work closely with civil engineers to recommend design alternatives that avoid, minimize and/or mitigate environmental impacts, including impacts to jurisdictional waters.

Analyze and prepare environmental documents and technical studies for CEQA/NEPA compliance, regulatory permitting, and MSHCP consistency.

Assist with AB52 Tribal consultations and related agreements and mitigation efforts.

Prepare RFPs for environmental consulting services; review consultant proposals, budgets and schedules; support consultant selection and oversee consultant deliverables and invoices.
Provide technical oversight for complex environmental review and recommend adaptive management solutions as needed.
Collaborate with internal staff, public agencies, consultants, non-profits, developers, and the public to ensure compliance and project delivery.
Lead or participate in field surveys, site assessments, and habitat, species, and nesting bird surveys to evaluate impacts and guide project planning, construction, maintenance, and mitigation site/ conservation lands management.

Graduation from an accredited college or university with a bachelor's degree, preferably with a major in environmental sciences, environmental engineering, urban or environmental planning, biological or ecological sciences, geography, archeology, hydrology, geology, chemistry, civil engineering, or a closely related field.

Two years of professional-level experience in one or more of the following areas: Environmental planning, regulatory compliance or natural resources management, or environmental engineering. (Experience working for or consulting to a public works agency is highly desirable.)

Experience preparing or reviewing technical studies, CEQA environmental documents (i.e., Environmental Impact Report, Mitigated Negative Declaration, Negative Declaration, Notice of Exemption).
Experience with preparing, reviewing or negotiating regulatory permits from California Department of Fish and Wildlife, Regional Water Quality Control Boards and US Army Corps of Engineers.

Position Description

This posting will be used to fill a full-time position in the Bureau of Watershed Protection and Restoration (BWPR) in the Department of Public Works.

This position serves as a key role within the BWPR managing technically complex stream and wetland restoration and stormwater projects from initiation thru construction.

This position will require the candidate to utilize their expertise in water resources and ecological related disciplines, including, but not limited to the following subjects: nature-based, stream and wetland restoration approaches; design analysis; stormwater management; surface water hydrology and hydraulic analysis; floodplain management; native plant community reestablishment; wildlife habitat restoration; review of engineering and construction plans, specifications and estimates; coordination with regulatory agencies; public outreach; easement acquisition; assistance in developing effective project permitting strategies; and, procurement and contract management.

The primary distinction of the Senior designation for a Project Manager is a manager's ability to manage projects of any size and complexity, provide mentorship and expertise to the staff, as well as assist with management duties for the Engineer Manager.

Nature And Variety Of Work

This position is responsible for managing the more challenging environmental restoration projects within the BWPR. The position is also responsible for developing scopes of work, assisting in the negotiation of the regulatory process, managing design/bidding processes, managing construction installation, and ensuring project performance.

This position serves as a professional resource to junior project management staff by sharing their greater level of knowledge and experience with challenging projects. Responsibilities also include assisting with mentoring and training junior project management staff.

The position works closely with other departments in the County, County officials, community representatives, design consultants, state and federal regulators, construction contractors, and the public-at-large for the purpose of presenting, explaining, and implementing various work projects.

The position involves regular work outside, including traversing steep grades, walking in streams and natural areas.

Examples Of Duties And Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Manages the design of complex stream and wetland restoration capital projects to assure completion on schedule and within budget. Provides for timely procurement of required consultant services. Develops schedule in keeping with established priorities. Routinely monitors consultant schedule maintenance and quality of product. Maintains effective communication with the project team. Monitors design progress to ensure maintenance of established budget.

Ensures that construction documents are complete and have the required detail to provide desired finished product. Provides for timely procurement of construction management services and establishes appropriate expectations for Construction Management performance to ensure quality, cost, and schedule controls. Provide sufficient field presence to ensure that established expectations are being met.

Prepares capital budget for assigned projects in accordance with established schedules and guidelines. Provides accurate construction cost estimates for new project requests and establishes milestones. Determines initial total project cost and probable funding sources. Allocates funding request based on realistic schedule projection. Provides sufficient back-up material to fully support requests.

Provides thorough and timely information through established reporting procedures and, as required, clearly conveys project status, schedule, problems, and action plans. Maintain accurate and current information in the County’s program management software (e-Builder).

Provides documentation for any significant changes in cost, schedule, or quality of projects. Provides information and recommended course of action on potential impacts to supervisory chain in time that direction for corrective action can be provided. Makes quality written or oral presentations of project status to higher management as required.

Provides technical assistance as required within area of nature-based, ecological restoration to supervisors, project managers, and other County agencies. Reviews and comments with timely response to requests for input. Serves on ad hoc technical review committees and provide well thought out recommendations.

Assists the Engineer Manager in maintaining effective development of and revision to working administrative and technical documents and to new product evaluation. Reviews and suggests improvements that will provide more efficient and higher quality work products such as policies and procedures and operating manuals. Provides suggestions for improvements in engineering standards for Design Manual and Standard Specifications and Details.

Performs related duties as assigned by the Engineer Manager.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Demonstrated experience in design and successful implementation of stream and wetland restoration projects, riparian enhancements, and related aquatic restoration projects with a strong ecological focus.

Demonstrated understanding of key ecological and geomorphological processes influencing stream and wetland ecosystems in Anne Arundel County.

Extensive knowledge of environmental restoration and/or engineering principles and practices related to capital project management and other program which involve defining the scope of work, contract requirements, cost estimation, budget analysis, managing contractor performance, and Federal, state, and local codes and regulations.

Thorough knowledge in evaluating consultant capabilities, bid proposals, project costs and scheduling, construction project bidding, change orders, and contractual requirements for payment.

Thorough knowledge in written, oral and electronic communications related to project management and consultant and contractor performance through concise and accurate reporting of technical details and construction status related to quality of work, time schedules, and cost estimates.

Ability to make effective technical presentations to diverse partners, including academic, local, state, federal, and non-governmental agencies and organizations.

Make presentations to community organizations and other citizens on capital projects relating to the scope of work, cost, schedule, purpose and need, and environmental trade-offs.

Proficiency with Google platform of tools and/or Microsoft Office software

Proficient knowledge of NPDES MS4 Permits and the Chesapeake Bay TMDL.

Proficient knowledge of stormwater management laws, rules and regulations in Maryland.

Excellent written and oral communication skills.

Ability to deal tactfully, effectively, and equitably with people.

Minimum Qualifications

Education:
A bachelor's degree from an accredited four-year college or university with a degree in engineering or a related field.

Experience
: Four (4) or more years' technical experience in engineering

Additional Requirements: A valid non-commercial Class C motor vehicle operator's license.

NOTE :
Related fields for the college-degree may include Environmental Engineering, Landscape Architecture, Fluvial Geomorphology, Environmental Science, Ecological Restoration, Natural Resources Management, or a similar field of study.

Extensive stream and wetland restoration design experience that took projects from site identification through permitted site plans.
Extensive experience obtaining local, state, and federal permits for stream and wetland restoration projects.
Experience with construction oversight on stream and wetland restoration projects.
Experience delineating jurisdictional wetlands and strong familiarity with USACE Section 404/401 permitting process.

Experience working with individual property owners, commercial properties, and/or HOAs to obtain rights of entry and/or easements.
Experience organizing and implementing long-term monitoring and maintenance associated with stream and wetland restoration projects.

Are you passionate about making a tangible difference in people's lives, protecting our environment while improving water quality? Join the City of Corona's Public Works team and play a vital role in shaping the future of our community! We're seeking a driven and journey level Environmental Compliance Coordinator to help with storm water management activities. Your expertise will directly contribute to the safety, well-being, and prosperity of our residents. If you're ready to leave your mark on a thriving community, we encourage you to apply!

We’re looking for an Environmental Compliance Coordinator to be part of our Environmental Services Group and help administer storm water activities. This is your chance to contribute towards adoption of a new Tri-County NPDES Permit, collaborating with Orange, Riverside, and San Bernardino counties, in addition to various City departments. Your expertise will drive the future of our community through implementation of the new Permit, ensuring City compliance for municipal facilities, construction sites, commercial/industrial facilities, and assisting staff on various capital improvement plan projects.

DEFINITION

Under general supervision, this position performs a variety of storm water and non-storm water compliance inspections and field work in conformance with the City's Storm Water Ordinance and National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) Permit for municipal facilities, construction sites, residential, and commercial and industrial businesses. Compliance and field work to include: erosion and sediment control; evaluation of existing site design, source and structural control Best Management Practices (BMPs) related to outdoor work and storage areas, vehicle and equipment fueling and maintenance, waste handling; delivery areas and loading docks; illicit and illegal connections to the City's storm/sewer drain systems; compliance with applicable construction standards, Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPP) and Water Quality Management Plans (WQMP); material inspection; and observation of construction of various treatment control BMPs during and post-construction. Other responsibilities may include: monitoring and sampling of storm water and non-storm water runoff; keeping project diaries; updating various databases; and coordinating with other City departments and agencies.

Knowledge & Education

Equivalent to an associate's degree in environmental science, biology or closely related field and five years work related experience in storm water management;

Or

High School Diploma and seven years experience in public works or environmental inspection with an emphasis in performing storm water compliance inspections.
Knowledge of City NPDES Ordinance and guidelines and regulations pertaining to local government operations, industrial storm water pollution prevention plans and BMPs for industrial facilities,
Knowledge of SWPPP goals and guidelines and regulations pertaining to local government operations, Federal Clean Water Act,
Knowledge of basic engineering concepts and practices and biological and chemical principals as related to water quality issues, sampling and laboratory methods, research techniques, public relations principles;
Knowledge of applicable federal, state and local laws, engineering plans, maps, legal descriptions, title reports, local ordinances and codes and department operating procedures;
Knowledge of methods, practices and procedures of mapping, drafting, specification development and other technical functions in support of a civil engineering office; permitting procedures; research techniques;

Ability to research property ownership, valuation and other legal matters;
Ability to prepare and update maps and engineering documents related to City infrastructure;
Ability to read, interpret, understand and prepare engineering records;
Ability to organize, file and maintain engineering records;
Ability to follow oral and written instructions; prepare and maintain notes, reports, maps, specifications and descriptions; make mathematical computations;
Ability to organize and prioritize tasks to meet deadlines;
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with staff, developers/contractors, consultants, business representatives, and the general public.

Possession of, or the ability to obtain, technical certification for Qualified SWPPP Practitioner (QSP) and one of the following:
Certificate as a Professional in Storm Water Quality (CPSWQ),
or Professional in Erosion and Sediment Control (CPESC),

Position Description

Position Overview:

The Harris County Fire Marshal's Office (HCFMO) is seeking a skilled and motivated Geographic Information System (GIS) Specialist to join the Operations Support Bureau. This role supports fire investigation, hazmat operations, emergency management, and multi-agency coordination through the development and maintenance of geospatial tools, data systems, internal GIS web applications, and analytical products.

The GIS Specialist will design, maintain, and analyze spatial datasets; produce maps, dashboards, and reports; and serve as the HCFMO's primary geospatial resource in support of operational, investigative, and strategic decision-making. The position interfaces regularly with fire, EMS, and law enforcement agency partners across Harris County, and may support Emergency Operations Center (EOC) events.

The ideal candidate is technically proficient in ESRI products, comfortable with data integration and automation, able to support configuration-level maintenance of internal mapping applications (e.g., layer setup, symbology, access/permissions settings), and capable of translating complex geospatial information into clear, actionable products for command staff, public officials, and partner agencies.

Duties and Responsibilities:

Geospatial Analysis & Decision Support
Perform spatial analysis to support fire investigation, hazmat incident response, deployment planning, prevention, and risk reduction activities.
Develop and maintain data layers and geodatabases integrating internal records (incident, investigation, inspection) with external datasets (county parcels, Census, CAD feeds, utility infrastructure).
Analyze incident patterns, coverage gaps, response time performance, and risk density to support strategic and operational planning by command staff.
Produce recommendations and briefings derived from geospatial analysis for use by the Fire Marshal, division leadership, and partner agencies.
Evaluate data and access requirements for internal geospatial applications and recommend configuration changes to layers, symbology, or user permissions to better support analytical and operational needs.

Data Management & Quality Assurance
Design, build, and maintain geodatabases from multiple internal and external data sources in various formats.
Ensure spatial data accuracy, integrity, and consistency through systematic quality control and error-checking procedures.
Maintain geospatial data feeds required by Computer-Aided Dispatch (CAD) systems used by the HCFMO and regional dispatch partners.
Develop and document data standards, coding structures, and metadata to support business continuity and interoperability.
Apply change-control practices (e.g., testing and validating configuration or data changes before deployment to production systems) to minimize disruption to operational users.
Support maintenance of user and facility access permissions within internal geospatial applications, ensuring data governance and access-control settings remain accurate and current.

Cartography & Application Management
Produce and maintain print and digital maps for fire investigation, hazmat operations, fire prevention, special events, and administrative use.
Create and maintain ArcGIS Online web maps, dashboards, Survey123 forms, and mobile mapping applications used by field personnel.
Provide geospatial products and field support during large-scale incidents.
Maintain and update the mobile mapping environment for fire investigators and inspectors.
Configure and maintain layer settings, symbology, and feature-service connections within HCFMO's internal geospatial application(s), coordinating with technical/IT staff as needed for deeper platform-level changes.

Reporting & Data Visualization
Design and maintain operational and strategic reports and dashboards tailored to varied audiences, from field supervisors to elected officials.
Translate complex spatial data into clear visualizations (maps, charts, heat maps, infographics) that support retention and informed decision-making.
Integrate GIS products with other software platforms to support enterprise data workflows.

Coordination & Consultation
Serve as the HCFMO's GIS representative in regional geospatial working groups and inter-agency coordination bodies.
Collaborate with HCFMO divisions (investigations, hazmat, fire prevention, operations) and partner agencies to identify GIS needs and solutions.
Provide technical consultation and training to HCFMO personnel on GIS tools, data applications, and spatial query methods.
Support integration of GIS capabilities with UAS (drone) operations for incident mapping, post-fire documentation, and aerial data collection.

Automation & Workflow Development
Develop Python scripts, Model Builder workflows, and other automation tools to streamline routine data processing and reporting.
Evaluate and recommend new geospatial technologies, extensions, and integrations to improve HCFMO workflows.
Document all procedures, scripts, and automated workflows to ensure knowledge continuity.

Bachelor's degree in Geographic Information Systems/Science, Geography, Computer Science, Emergency Management, or a closely related field

Experience creating and maintaining geodatabases and ensuring geospatial data quality and integrity.
Experience producing maps, dashboards, and analytical reports for operational or decision-making purposes.

ESRI product suite: ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online/Enterprise, and extensions.
Geodatabase design, maintenance, and spatial data quality assurance methods.
Statistical and analytical methods applicable to spatial data (clustering, network analysis, proximity, density).
CAD system geospatial data requirements and integration methods.
Emergency management frameworks including ICS/NIMS; EOC operations and GISS function.
GPS concepts and field data collection procedures.
Data governance and access-control principles as applied to enterprise GIS applications.
Perform complex spatial analysis to support tactical, operational, and strategic decision-making in a public safety environment.
Produce clear, accurate, and audience-appropriate maps, reports, and visualizations under time pressure.
Manage multiple concurrent projects and prioritize effectively in a dynamic, operational environment.

Work independently with minimal supervision while maintaining alignment with organizational priorities.

new_jobs.title: GIS Specialist
new_jobs.description:
Ting Internet is a leading fiber Internet provider in the United States, delivering future-proof internet in over a dozen Ting Towns across the country.
As part of Tucows (NASDAQ:TCX, TSX:TC), Ting is backed by outstanding resources and talent. We embrace a people-first philosophy that is rooted in respect, trust, and flexibility. We believe that whatever works for our employees is what works best for us. 
The work we do genuinely changes lives. If this sounds exciting, we’d love to hear from you!
Position Overview
As a fixed-line Fiber provider, Ting relies on knowing where our customers are and where our fiber is so we can bring those two things together. GIS (Geographic Information Systems) is all about modelling real-world objects as data that other digital systems can work with. Your job as a GIS Specialist is to ensure the data in these systems does match the real world, and then use this data to answer business questions.
Key Responsibilities
Manage the GIS ticket queue to support our internal users Solve suspected data issues such as address availability check errors by looking at plant drawings, maps, aerial and street photographs, and other sources of data to determine if our system might have the wrong data. Correct as necessary, or confirm an unexpected case is in fact accurate.
Add newly created addresses. If a building adds an apartment, or a new building is constructed on an empty lot, the new address needs to be added to our system.

Audit partner address releases Our partner providers invoice us for passed addresses, serviced addresses, and other incremental services that need to be checked against what they have actually provided to us. Using reports, tracking sheets, and automation tools that you will help to design, ensure that our numbers match their numbers.
Receive address delivery batches from partners when new areas are constructed. This data must be checked and ingested into our database so customers can place orders.  We also need to track releases so we can account for the pro-rated invoice the following month. Partner deliveries also need to be checked against map data to ensure they didn’t deliver addresses that don’t exist, or deliver the same one twice.

As-Built and Records Maintenance Ingest as-built records from partner and organic construction into our systems of record. Convert from various CAD formats to structured data formats that can be ingested by IQGeo and other systems.
Maintain the data sets in IQGeo and other systems in response to network changes, additional plant placements, and otherwise ensure that our system of record always reflects the actual state of our plant, and the plant of our partner networks.

Periodic Tasks: Work with the design team to correctly update IQGeo with plant moves or other changes to the physical network that need to be reflected back here.
Twice a year, produce output to support our FCC reporting. This process is very automatable, but it still requires human judgment to define how the process should work and to ensure our filings happen accurately. On a different twice-annual basis, download the aggregated FCC data that becomes publicly available and ingest it back into our database so we can use it for business intelligence.
Use database queries and other geospatial tools to generate reports for internal stakeholders.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities 
Geography was actually fun for you. Maybe you enjoy looking at maps and exploring real places without leaving your desk.
Attention to detail! This is the most important skill, as the accuracy of our data affects every downstream process.
Familiarity with IQGeo. This is the main tool used by the GIS team for viewing plant data and the addresses we manage (organic, partners with no system of their own). This is a fairly intuitive web-based tool, but has some nuances to it.
Experience with SQL queries, especially PostGIS. Our underlying database is PostGIS. Being able to construct an SQL query to produce aggregate data or work with batches can save a great deal of manual work.
Experience with other GIS tools such as ArcGIS Pro. This is another ancillary tool used to store map layers and do other data aggregations. Not strictly necessary, but a nice-to-have.
You like to help others, but not necessarily be on the front-lines of customer service. You will be supporting Ting people internally only.
You are a good self-starter and can work independently. The work is largely asynchronous, but we need to provide a high service level to our internal customers and make sure nothing falls through the cracks.
You have the tenacity to get work done, but are just lazy enough to look at repetitive tasks and think about how better tools could take the grunt work out of it.

Qualifications  Completed Post-secondary education in Applied Geography, Geographic Information Systems or equivalent experience
Industry and GIS/CAD specific certifications and training preferred
3+ years of GIS/AutoCAD/Network documentation system experience
2+ years of demonstrated experience with spatial data, data entry and conversion
2+ years demonstrated outstanding project management skills
Programming experience with Go, Python, and PostGIS an asset

Are you looking to make a difference and join a highly motivated team working on issues critical to ensuring the safety and sustainability of California? The Office of Energy Infrastructure Safety’s Environmental Science Division is seeking an Environmental Scientist to analyze performance with vegetation management commitments in electrical utility Wildfire Mitigation Plans (WMP).

The Environmental Science Division is responsible for evaluating the vegetation management aspects of utility WMPs, assessing performance in meeting vegetation management-related commitments described in the WMPs, and ensuring that each utility is reducing its risk of igniting a catastrophic wildfire. To this end, Division scientists review regulatory filings and utility procedures, analyze reported data, perform audits, conduct field inspections, publish findings, and engage with the utilities and interested parties. Incumbent will also conduct investigations into concerns raised by external parties regarding potential WMP findings, conduct critical and/or sensitive scientific investigations and studies and prepare guidance, policy, planning, or regulatory documents on issues of importance to the department as assigned. Incumbent will identify issues found in the field and elevate to the Supervisor with proposed recommendations. The incumbent will develop and maintain positive relationships with internal and external agency partners. The incumbent will be a subject matter expert on vegetation management inspection programs to assess electrical utility performance with approved WMPs and other regulatory requirements of the Department associated with forestry, wildfire science, climate change and the environment.

As a Ground Support Crew Member, you keep the network running. You will be based in Northridge, working across our active delivery sites, preparing aircraft, loading orders, and acting as the link between our part 135 Operations Partner and the restaurants and shops our drones fly for. This is a hands-on, field-based role with real responsibility from day one.

Your shift starts before the first flight. You inspect the aircraft, verify equipment, and communicate with the remote ops center to begin the day. When an order comes in from a partner restaurant or shop, you make it happen and see the flight off.

In this role, you will:

Support the launch of new operations sites, including onboarding new customers and enrolling them in our delivery program
Conduct pre- and post-flight aircraft inspections per approved procedures; maintain accurate airworthiness and maintenance records
Prepare and load payloads for each flight; verify order accuracy and packaging integrity at the point of handoff from merchant partners
Operate and service ground equipment and charging systems
Act as the on-site liaison between remote operations center and partner restaurants and shops, coordinating flight schedules, communicating delays, and resolving ground-level issues in real time
Troubleshoot and document mechanical and electrical discrepancies; escalate faults through the proper maintenance release process
Enforce site safety protocols, manage non-crew personnel around the aircraft, and report occurrences through Safety Management System
Complete Operator certification and all required recurrent training to maintain active status

Requirements

FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate (current and valid)
Hands-on experience with mechanical and/or electrical systems; aviation, automotive, robotics, or industrial background all considered
Ability to follow and execute written SOPs accurately in a safety-critical environment
Clear communicator; comfortable coordinating between a remote operations team and on-site merchant partners
Comfortable working outdoors, on your feet, across variable shift hours including early mornings and weekends
Ability to comply with the Company's FAA/DOT-mandated drug and alcohol testing program (see Drug & Alcohol Testing below)
Based or able to work onsite in Los Angeles, CA

Preferred qualifications:

Multi-rotor UAS operating experience beyond Part 107 certification
Experience in a Part 135, Part 145, or other FAA-regulated operating environment
Experience authoring or revising controlled documents (SOPs, maintenance procedures, inspection checklists)
Manned aviation background (student pilot, PPL, CPL, or military flight experience)

Work Environment

This is an on-site, field-based role operating from Ground Control Stations and active delivery sites in and around Northridge (Los Angeles, CA)
The work will be predominately outdoors with exposure to sun, heat, wind, cold, and noise for the duration of a shift.
Shifts may include early mornings, weekends, holidays, and on-call availability
Travel will be required between local operating sites and to support new route validation

The physical demands described below are representative of those that must be met to successfully perform the essential functions of this role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these functions.

Stand, walk, and remain on your feet for the majority of a shift, often on outdoor and uneven surfaces
Frequently lift, carry, and position aircraft, batteries, payloads, and ground equipment weighing up to approximately 50 lbs; occasionally more with assistance
Bend, stoop, kneel, crouch, and reach to inspect aircraft, load payloads, and service ground equipment
Use hand tools and perform tasks requiring manual dexterity and fine motor control
Sufficient near and distance visual acuity and hearing to inspect aircraft, monitor operations, and communicate on-site and by radio
Communicate clearly and exchange accurate information verbally and in writing with the Air Operations team and merchant partners

The Riverside County Flood Control and Water Conservation District seeks an Regulatory and Environmental Planner (Associate Environmental Specialist). This position is assigned to the Regulatory Division in Riverside and is comparable to traditional Environmental Planner roles.

To learn more about this position click here to view a video.

Individuals in this role will have prior planning experience and will support the District with a broad range of responsibilities related to environmental compliance under laws such as the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), the Clean Water Act, the state and federal Endangered Species Acts, and the California Fish and Game Code. Key duties include performing and reviewing technical analyses for flood control projects to assess environmental impacts; conducting field survey; and recommending appropriate mitigation measures in accordance with applicable environmental regulations and procedures.

Additional responsibilities include preparing and reviewing environmental documents (e.g., CEQA analyses), as well as regulatory permit applications under Sections 404, 401, and 1600. Associate Regulatory and Environmental Planners may also be tasked with developing Requests for Proposals (RFPs), overseeing consultant deliverables, and coordinating with internal divisions and external agencies at the local, state, federal, or tribal level. The ideal candidate will have experience serving as a project manager or task lead in a similar role at an environmental or engineering focused consulting firm or within a public works or land use/planning agency, and a background in preparing or reviewing technical studies, including NEPA or CEQA environmental documents (e.g., Environmental Impact Reports, Mitigated Negative Declarations, Negative Declarations, Notices of Exemption). Experience in preparing, reviewing, or negotiating regulatory permits from the California Department of Fish and Wildlife, Regional Water Quality Control Boards, and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers is highly desirable. Familiarity with projects located within the Western Riverside County Multiple Species Habitat Conservation Plan (MSHCP) and/or the Coachella Valley MSHCP is also preferred.

The most competitive candidates will demonstrate a solid understanding of the principles and practices of urban and environmental planning, flood control, and land development. They should have experience interpreting and implementing relevant environmental laws and regulations, including CEQA, the National Historic Preservation Act, Assembly Bill 52 (AB 52), the Federal and California Endangered Species Acts, the Clean Water Act (Sections 401 and 404), and the California Fish and Game Code. Incumbents in this track assist with CEQA compliance, species and habitat management, regulatory permitting acquisition, negotiation and compliance, prepare or review environmental documents and technical studies, and coordinate with internal staff, public agencies, consultants, and other stakeholders as needed to ensure effective project delivery.

To learn more about the position or the Regulatory Division at the District, here.

The Riverside County Flood Control and Water Conservation District provides for the control and conservation of flood and storm waters and for the protection of watercourses, watersheds, public highways, life and property from damage within its boundaries.

The primary distinction of the Senior designation for a Project Manager is a manager's ability to manage projects of any size and complexity, provide mentorship and expertise to the staff, as well as assist with management duties for the Engineer Manager.

This position serves as a professional resource to junior project management staff by sharing their greater level of knowledge and experience with challenging projects. Responsibilities also include assisting with mentoring and training junior project management staff.

The position works closely with other departments in the County, County officials, community representatives, design consultants, state and federal regulators, construction contractors, and the public-at-large for the purpose of presenting, explaining, and implementing various work projects.

The position involves regular work outside, including traversing steep grades, walking in streams and natural areas.

Manages the design of complex stream and wetland restoration capital projects to assure completion on schedule and within budget. Provides for timely procurement of required consultant services. Develops schedule in keeping with established priorities. Routinely monitors consultant schedule maintenance and quality of product. Maintains effective communication with the project team. Provide sufficient field presence to ensure that established expectations are being met.

Prepares capital budget for assigned projects in accordance with established schedules and guidelines. Provides accurate construction cost estimates for new project requests and establishes milestones. Determines initial total project cost and probable funding sources. Allocates funding request based on realistic schedule projection. Provides sufficient back-up material to fully support requests.

Provides thorough and timely information through established reporting procedures and, as required, clearly conveys project status, schedule, problems, and action plans. Maintain accurate and current information in the County’s program management software (e-Builder).

Provides documentation for any significant changes in cost, schedule, or quality of projects. Provides information and recommended course of action on potential impacts to supervisory chain in time that direction for corrective action can be provided. Makes quality written or oral presentations of project status to higher management as required.

Provides technical assistance as required within area of nature-based, ecological restoration to supervisors, project managers, and other County agencies. This is your chance to contribute towards adoption of a new Tri-County NPDES Permit, collaborating with Orange, Riverside, and San Bernardino counties, in addition to various City departments. Your expertise will drive the future of our community through implementation of the new Permit, ensuring City compliance for municipal facilities, construction sites, commercial/industrial facilities, and assisting staff on various capital improvement plan projects.

DEFINITION

Under general supervision, this position performs a variety of storm water and non-storm water compliance inspections and field work in conformance with the City's Storm Water Ordinance and National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Municipal Separate Storm Sewer System (MS4) Permit for municipal facilities, construction sites, residential, and commercial and industrial businesses. Compliance and field work to include: erosion and sediment control; evaluation of existing site design, source and structural control Best Management Practices (BMPs) related to outdoor work and storage areas, vehicle and equipment fueling and maintenance, waste handling; delivery areas and loading docks; illicit and illegal connections to the City's storm/sewer drain systems; compliance with applicable construction standards, Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPP) and Water Quality Management Plans (WQMP); material inspection; and observation of construction of various treatment control BMPs during and post-construction. Other responsibilities may include: monitoring and sampling of storm water and non-storm water runoff; keeping project diaries; updating various databases; and coordinating with other City departments and agencies.

Knowledge & Education

Equivalent to an associate's degree in environmental science, biology or closely related field and five years work related experience in storm water management;

High School Diploma and seven years experience in public works or environmental inspection with an emphasis in performing storm water compliance inspections.
Knowledge of City NPDES Ordinance and guidelines and regulations pertaining to local government operations, industrial storm water pollution prevention plans and BMPs for industrial facilities,

Knowledge of basic engineering concepts and practices and biological and chemical principals as related to water quality issues, sampling and laboratory methods, research techniques, public relations principles;
Knowledge of applicable federal, state and local laws, engineering plans, maps, legal descriptions, title reports, local ordinances and codes and department operating procedures;

Ability to read, interpret, understand and prepare engineering records;

Certificate as a Professional in Storm Water Quality (CPSWQ),
or Professional in Erosion and Sediment Control (CPESC),
or Certified Erosion Sediment and Storm Water Inspector (CESSWI) within twelve (12) months of appointment.

Possession of, or the ability to obtain a technical certification for Qualified Industrial Stormwater Practitioner (QISP) within eighteen (18) months of appointment is desirable.

With a strong pipeline of confirmed work moving into 2026, we have an opportunity for several Site Engineers (Geo-environmental) to join our team. The successful candidate will play a key role in the day-to-day delivery of projects, working closely with and being supported by team members, project managers and project directors. Activities will typically include groundwater monitoring and supervision of contractors (e.g. drill rigs).

The role will be predominately site based. Site works are dependent on active projects with travel to and working on sites across the whole of the UK.

The post will be within our Ground & Water team which is a service line in WSP's Earth & Environment business.

Supervision of site investigations.

The successful candidate will be enthusiastic, practically minded, confident and self-motivated, with excellent verbal and written communication skills. Having flexibility working within a team setting is essential.

Site safety qualifications (e.g. first aid training and site supervisors safety training scheme (SSSTS) or equivalent) is desirable.
Relevant technical degree is desirable but not essential e.g. chemistry, biology, geology, engineering, or environmental science
